title: The Quiet Push
briefing.company: Mercadito is a marketplace: thousands of small shops, one checkout. Orders go from the storefront to checkout-api, which calls the cart, the payments database and an external payment gateway that someone else runs.
briefing.role: You're on call for checkout this week. It's Thursday. Nobody else is awake, which is the whole point of you.
change.deployCart: cart-api 3.8.1: dependency bumps, no behavior change
change.promoFlag: promo banner on for the morning campaign
change.timeout: align payment timeout with the provider's SLA doc (8s)
runbook.checkoutLatency.title: Checkout latency is high
runbook.checkoutLatency.body:
Checkout latency is the sum of its dependencies. Before touching anything, find out which one got slower and when.

First, look at what changed: deploys, config pushes and flags in the last hours. Most nights, the answer is in that list.

Then split the time: server latency for checkout-api against client latency for each call it makes. The call that grew is the suspect. Its timeouts and retries decide how long a customer waits.

Restarting checkout-api clears in-flight requests and nothing else. Use it only if you know why.
runbook.paymentGw.title: payment-gw (external provider)
runbook.paymentGw.body:
payment-gw is run by an outside provider. We see it only through our own client metrics and spans: there are no server-side signals.

Every night between 02:30 and 05:00 the provider runs settlement. During that window a few percent of authorize calls hang for nine seconds or more. They don't fail; they just never answer in time.

The provider recommends a client timeout of 1 s or less with one retry. A short timeout turns a hung call into a fast retry that almost always succeeds.

A word on retries: a client that gave up waiting does not know the provider didn't charge the card. A safe retry needs an idempotency key, a fixed number of attempts and a total time budget. Without them, a short timeout turns a slow night into double charges, or into more load on a provider that is already struggling.

prompt.lucia.ask: The morning team in Bogotá is asking why checkout feels slow. Are we losing orders? What do I tell them?
factor.timeoutRaised: A config change raised the payment client timeout from 800 ms to 8 s.
factor.gwSlowTail: During its nightly settlement window, the payment gateway leaves about 7% of calls hanging.
factor.unguardedConfig: Config changes reach every instance at once, with no canary and no bounds check.
distractor.cartDeploy: Tonight's cart-api deploy introduced a regression.
distractor.promoBanner: The promo banner flag added load to the storefront.
chain.unguarded: Config pushes skip canaries and bounds checks
chain.change: 03:03 · config v413: payment timeout 800 ms → 8 s
chain.settlement: payment-gw settlement window: ~7% of calls hang
chain.waiting: Hung calls now wait 8 s before the retry, not 0.8 s
chain.customers: Customers wait 8 s or more to pay; some give up
debrief.chainNote: The short timeout used to hide the gateway's bad nights: a hung call failed fast and the retry went through. Raising it turned a hidden condition into a visible one. The person who pushed it read a real document and made a reasonable change; the system let it reach every instance at once.
variant.a.change.deploy: checkout-api 2.13.2: fix typos in the receipt email
variant.b.change.config: receipt email template r7 for the campaign
variant.b.change.deploy: checkout-api 2.14.0: tax lines computed per item for the new invoicing rules
variant.b.factor.regression: A checkout-api deploy made every order spend about two seconds in checkout-api's own code.
variant.b.factor.inRequest: The new work runs inside the order request, while cart-api, payments-db and payment-gw stay fast.
variant.b.factor.unguardedDeploy: Deploys reach every checkout-api instance in one step, with no canary stage.
variant.b.chain.unguarded: Deploys skip canaries: a release reaches all four instances at once
variant.b.chain.inRequest: The new work runs inside every order request
variant.b.chain.selfTime: Each order spends ~2 s in checkout-api's own code; its calls stay fast
variant.b.chain.customers: Every customer waits seconds longer to pay
variant.b.debriefNote: Nothing behind checkout-api got slower: the cart, the database and the gateway answered in their usual time, and the extra seconds were checkout-api's own. A release that changes how each order is built changes every order. Going out to all four instances at once meant every customer met it at the same moment, and taking it back was the only fix.
variant.c.change.config: bigger batches for the nightly order export
variant.c.change.deploy: checkout-api 2.14.1: fix rounding in receipt totals
variant.c.factor.stockCheck: The promo flag turned on a stock check for every order line, and checkout-api runs it on its own CPU.
variant.c.factor.cpuSaturated: checkout-api's CPU is pinned near 100%, so orders queue for a free worker.
variant.c.factor.fixedCapacity: checkout-api runs a fixed four instances: autoscaling is off and nothing adds capacity.
variant.c.chain.change: 02:56 · promo flag on: a stock check per order line
variant.c.chain.queue: Orders queue for a free worker
variant.c.chain.customers: Some customers wait 5 s or more to pay
variant.c.debriefNote: The flag looked like a storefront change, but it turned on work inside checkout-api for every order line. Four instances had no room for it: the CPU pinned and orders waited for a worker. Rolling back the config or the release could not help, because neither caused it. More instances gave the extra work somewhere to run; making that work fit is the follow-up.
variant.d.change.config: keep idempotency keys for 2 h, per the provider's retry window
variant.d.change.deploy: checkout-api 2.13.0: cache tax rules in process
variant.d.factor.leak: A checkout-api deploy leaks memory; the heap has grown since that release went out.
variant.d.factor.gcPauses: With the heap that full, garbage collection pauses stall orders, and they get longer every minute.
variant.d.factor.noSoak: Releases only get a five-minute smoke test and nothing alerts on checkout-api memory, so a slow leak ships unseen.
variant.d.chain.noSoak: Releases get a five-minute smoke test; nothing watches memory
variant.d.chain.heap: The heap grows about 9 MB a minute, all night
variant.d.chain.gc: GC pauses stall orders, longer every minute
variant.d.chain.customers: Customers wait longer and longer to pay
variant.d.debriefNote: The leak started with the 23:20 release and grew for hours before anyone could feel it. A restart frees the heap, which is why it looks like a fix: the alert goes quiet, then the pauses come back. Only the rollback removes the code that leaks; a five-minute smoke test was never going to see it.
